what_it_does: This paper presents an ultra-low-power Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE) radio chip for wearables and IoT. BLE radios must rapidly hop between frequency channels (every few milliseconds) to avoid interference, and they use a modulation scheme (GFSK) that requires stable frequency control. The new design uses a digital Phase-Locked Loop (a circuit that locks onto a reference frequency)—instead of the analog approaches in traditional radios—and optimizes it to switch frequencies in under 20 microseconds while burning only 380 microwatts of power. This makes wearable BLE devices run much longer on a small battery.
